newsitem.title: UK: BAA SHARES CUSHIONED BY RECORD TRAFFIC DATA.
newsitem.headline: BAA SHARES CUSHIONED BY RECORD TRAFFIC DATA.

text.p: Shares in British airports operator BAA Plc were slightly lower on Wednesday, cushioned by better than expected traffic figures for July, dealers said.
By 0830 GMT, BAA shares were off 2p at 583-1/2p.
"They were better than expected traffic figures...but what the stock does depends on the rest of the market," one trader said.
The FTSE 100 was off 26 points or 0.51 percent at 5,049.8, tracking the sharp Wall Street sell-off overnight.
BAA said its seven UK airports handled 10.2 million passengers in July, up six percent on the same month last year and the highest number ever recorded in a single month.
It was the first time BAA has handled more than 100 million passengers in a 12-month period, the group said.
Despite the British Airways strike, every airport and all of the major markets recorded increases, it said.
British Airways shares were up 6p at 637p.
BAA also said that the volume of air cargo tonnage was unaffected by the British Airways cabin crew strike.
